kinds.definition: A choice about how a metric is defined or which grain it uses
kinds.control: A step that removes a bias or distortion
kinds.caveat: A stated limit on what the numbers can show
kinds.segmentation: A way of cutting the population
kinds.presentation: A storytelling or layout technique that shapes how numbers are read

concepts.name: Save-rate denominator choice
concepts.description: Save rate is computed over all sessions or over resolved sessions only. The two differ by the no-outcome share, which can be close to half of sessions.
concepts.why: Save rates from different reports are not comparable until the denominator is known.

concepts.name: Counterfactual uplift at prior rate
concepts.description: Apply the earlier period's rate to the current period's volume and report the difference as incremental outcomes.
concepts.why: Turns a rate change into a count the business can value.

concepts.name: Matched-length window
concepts.description: Compare a partial period only against the same number of days at the start of the prior period.
concepts.why: Stops a partial quarter from looking like a decline.

concepts.name: Period-over-period delta
concepts.description: Show each KPI with its change against the prior equal window, as a percent or percentage-point badge.
concepts.why: The standard read for pulse reports.

concepts.name: Trailing window snapshot
concepts.description: Report the last 30 or 60 days against the 30 or 60 days before.
concepts.why: Keeps a recurring report current without waiting for calendar periods to close.

concepts.name: Full weeks only
concepts.description: Weekly trends drop the current partial week.
concepts.why: A partial week reads as a false drop at the right edge of a chart.

concepts.name: Store-timezone bucketing
concepts.description: All dates are bucketed in the store's timezone.
concepts.why: UTC bucketing shifts late-evening orders into the next day and breaks reconciliation with Shopify.

concepts.name: Bulk-operation exclusion
concepts.description: Identify merchant bulk cancellations per subscription from the audit log and remove them, keeping organic cancellations on the same days.
concepts.why: Administrative clean-ups otherwise read as churn spikes.

concepts.name: Organic vs reported pairing
concepts.description: Show every growth figure twice, as reported and with administrative events removed.
concepts.why: Lets the reader see both the platform number and the business number.

concepts.name: Event anomaly check
concepts.description: State whether bulk actions or one-off events appear in the trend window before calling growth organic.
concepts.why: Stops a one-off event being read as a trend.

concepts.name: Retention from own start date
concepts.description: Measure each subscriber's retention from their own start date rather than from a calendar date.
concepts.why: Makes cohorts of different sizes and timing comparable.

concepts.name: Observability truncation
concepts.description: Cut the cohort window so every member can be observed for the full checkpoint length.
concepts.why: Keeps denominators complete at each checkpoint.

concepts.name: Maturity filter
concepts.description: Restrict to subscriptions at least 90 days old before comparing cancellation shares.
concepts.why: Young groups have not had time to churn.

concepts.name: Youth bias
concepts.description: New products, intervals or offers show low cancellation because their subscribers are young.
concepts.why: Share-still-active flatters anything launched recently.

concepts.name: Survivorship bias
concepts.description: A group defined by a later action, such as changing interval or skipping, is pre-filtered for people who stayed long enough to act.
concepts.why: Makes the action look causal for retention when it is not.

concepts.name: Administrative cancels treated as survivors
concepts.description: Bulk-cancelled subscriptions count as surviving in retention curves because the customer did not cancel.
concepts.why: Stops clean-ups from lowering measured retention.

concepts.name: In-flight cohort exclusion
concepts.description: Exclude dunning entry cohorts that still have many open cases, because fast recoveries resolve first.
concepts.why: Open cohorts flatter the recovery rate.

concepts.name: Dunning by entry cohort
concepts.description: Group dunning windows by the quarter they opened in and report outcomes once resolved.
concepts.why: Links recovery to the period the failures happened.

concepts.name: Subscriber-level recovery
concepts.description: Count recovery once per subscriber rather than per dunning window.
concepts.why: Gives a different rate from window-level counting.

concepts.name: Tenure segmentation
concepts.description: Cut cancel-flow outcomes by the billing cycle the subscriber was on, or by grouped tenure bands.
concepts.why: Save receptiveness changes sharply with tenure.

concepts.name: Reason segmentation
concepts.description: Cut save rate by the cancel-survey reason.
concepts.why: Shows which reasons an offer can address.

concepts.name: Treatment attribution
concepts.description: Attribute each save to the offer that closed it, such as skip or discount.
concepts.why: Shows which offers do the work and at what cost.

concepts.name: Repeat-attempt analysis
concepts.description: Count how many subscribers enter the cancel flow more than once.
concepts.why: A save that is followed by a second attempt did not stick.

concepts.name: MRR run-rate valuation
concepts.description: Value sessions at the subscription's monthly run-rate at the moment of the session. The June page states this is velocity, not lifetime damage.
concepts.why: MRR at risk is not revenue lost; realised revenue after save is the complement.

concepts.name: Baseline lift index
concepts.description: Divide event-window revenue by the baseline daily rate times the event length.
concepts.why: Compares products of different size on the same scale.

concepts.name: Per-day run-rate
concepts.description: Divide counts by days so windows of different length compare.
concepts.why: Needed for event windows and partial periods.

concepts.name: Classification rubric
concepts.description: Label each row with a verdict pill such as winner, sleeper, underperformer, anchor or too new to call.
concepts.why: Turns a table into a decision list. The rubric's thresholds are rarely stated.

concepts.name: Offer cohorting
concepts.description: Group subscriptions by the discount code or offer they started on, with the offer's active window.
concepts.why: Links acquisition offers to retention quality.

concepts.name: Pack-size economics
concepts.description: Compare cycles, cancellation and lifetime revenue by quantity per line.
concepts.why: Tests whether larger packs are worth steering toward.

concepts.name: Interval economics
concepts.description: Compare cycles, cancellation and lifetime revenue by delivery interval.
concepts.why: More cycles on a short interval can still mean less value.

concepts.name: Interval migration matrix
concepts.description: Cross opt-in interval with current interval to see who changes cadence and in which direction.
concepts.why: Shows whether the signup choice is permanent.

concepts.name: Opt-in interval from selling plan
concepts.description: Take opt-in interval from the selling plan on the earliest line and current interval from the live delivery policy, normalised to days.
concepts.why: Skio stores the two in different places.

concepts.name: Category from titles and tags
concepts.description: Derive product category by parsing product titles or tags.
concepts.why: Skio has no category field, so every report builds its own.

concepts.name: Post-event cumulative cancellation
concepts.description: Track the share cancelled by 7, 14, 30, 60 and 180 days after a trigger event.
concepts.why: Finds the window where an intervention should land.

concepts.name: Frequency dose-response
concepts.description: Bucket subscribers by how often they used a feature and compare outcomes across buckets.
concepts.why: A monotone pattern suggests, but does not prove, a real effect.

concepts.name: Recurring orders via billing attempts
concepts.description: Identify recurring orders from successful billing attempts (errorCode IS NULL) linked to the store's subscriptions, because Order.subscriptionId is empty.
concepts.why: Recurring revenue cannot be read from the order table directly.

concepts.name: Revenue exclusions
concepts.description: Exclude cancelled and deleted orders from revenue.
concepts.why: Keeps revenue in line with Shopify net figures.

concepts.name: Revenue-mix decomposition
concepts.description: Split revenue into first-time, recurring and one-time and show each as a share of total.
concepts.why: Shows whether subscription is gaining share, independent of total growth.

concepts.name: Variant decomposition
concepts.description: Break a product's revenue and activations down by plan length or variant with share bars.
concepts.why: Shows whether prepaid plans or monthly plans carry the product.

concepts.name: Launch-window snapshot
concepts.description: Report a short launch window day by day with store totals and product spotlights.
concepts.why: Gives a fast read before cohorts mature.

concepts.name: External benchmark reference
concepts.description: Compare a rate against an industry range.
concepts.why: None of the catalogued reports cite a source for their benchmark ranges.

concepts.name: Subset reconciliation note
concepts.description: Flag when a breakdown covers a different population from the headline total.
concepts.why: Stops a subset from being read as the whole.

concepts.name: Data-hygiene check
concepts.description: Check for migration or import artefacts, for example by confirming every subscription has a completed cycle and one-day mortality is normal.
concepts.why: Imported or purged subscriptions distort every rate.

concepts.name: Causal-limits statement
concepts.description: State that nothing was randomised and period differences reflect everything that changed.
concepts.why: Stops before-and-after comparisons being read as proof.

concepts.name: Holdout test recommendation
concepts.description: Recommend a randomised slice with a control group before shipping a change suggested by observational data.
concepts.why: The only way past survivorship and confounding.

concepts.name: Grain choice
concepts.description: Counts are taken at the subscription, subscriber, line or session grain.
concepts.why: Totals at different grains do not reconcile, for example line counts exceed subscription counts.

concepts.name: Re-check schedule
concepts.description: List what to re-pull and when, such as after quarter close or once cohorts mature.
concepts.why: Turns open questions into a follow-up plan.

concepts.name: Animated replay
concepts.description: Replay a month day by day with one particle per session, order faithful and pacing dramatised, with heavier days slowed down.
concepts.why: High emotional impact. Pacing is not proportional to time, which the page discloses.

concepts.name: Single-cycle hazard
concepts.description: For each cycle, divide cancellations during that cycle by everyone who reached it.
concepts.why: Unlike active vs cumulative cancelled counts, it is not distorted by how fast the base has grown.

concepts.name: Stock vs cumulative-flow mixing
concepts.description: Comparing today's active count in a bucket against all-time cancellations from that bucket.
concepts.why: In a growing account the newest buckets hold people too new to cancel, so their cancel rate looks low and later buckets look worse. Seen in a first draft that a later version corrected.

concepts.name: Right-censoring
concepts.description: Subscribers still inside a window have not had the chance to reach the outcome. Their buckets are incomplete, not zero.
concepts.why: Young flows and young cohorts under-report later-stage outcomes.

concepts.name: Pacing projection
concepts.description: Scale a partial-period total by total days over elapsed days.
concepts.why: Gives a quick full-period read. Seasonality inside the period makes it biased.

concepts.name: Source cross-check
concepts.description: Check a warehouse field against raw orders and switch source when it fails.
concepts.why: A warehouse revenue field can disagree with raw orders for some merchants; switching source avoids false spikes.

concepts.name: Price-driver check
concepts.description: Check average price by cycle to rule out a post-intro price step before blaming churn on product fit.
concepts.why: Rules out the most common mechanical cause of a cycle-2 cliff.

concepts.name: Basket pairing
concepts.description: Count subscribers holding each pair of products.
concepts.why: Reveals variety-stacking behaviour a bundle could formalise.

concepts.name: Reason-capture audit
concepts.description: Measure how many sessions actually record a reason before trusting reason breakdowns.
concepts.why: A 5% capture sample cannot support reason-level decisions.

concepts.name: Versioned correction
concepts.description: Reissue a report with a corrected method and a footnote that explains what the earlier draft got wrong.
concepts.why: Keeps the audit trail visible to the reader.

concepts.name: Flow-structure audit
concepts.description: Map each reason to its treatment steps and check for dead ends, mismatched reasons and missing actions such as pause or delay.
concepts.why: A flow with one offer per reason cannot save people the first offer does not fit.

concepts.name: Save durability
concepts.description: Track whether a saved subscription is still active N days after the save.
concepts.why: A save that reverses in 30 days is a delayed cancellation.

concepts.name: Splash-screen intervention
concepts.description: An offer shown before the reason step, usually skip next order.
concepts.why: Can dominate save counts while producing low-durability saves.

concepts.name: Treatment-type scoping
concepts.description: Define the analysis by Skio session status such as SAVED_BY_SKIP or SAVED_BY_PAUSE, and confirm each exists before analysing it.
concepts.why: A treatment that is not configured returns zero sessions, which is a setup fact, not a result.

concepts.name: Reorder attribution via line items
concepts.description: Count a recurring order after a skip only when it is tied to the same subscription line through OrderLineItem to SubscriptionLine.
concepts.why: Order-level joins attribute unrelated orders to the skip.

concepts.name: Filter verification
concepts.description: Before trusting a filtered breakdown, run it with two different filter values and confirm the outputs differ and the parts sum to the unfiltered total.
concepts.why: Some chart filters silently return unfiltered data with no error.

concepts.name: Trusted-chart control
concepts.description: When a chart returns zero rows, re-run a chart you trust over the identical window before concluding anything.
concepts.why: Separates a broken query or wrong merchant from a real instrumentation gap or a later data start date.

concepts.name: No forced reconciliation
concepts.description: Show each source's number labelled by source and name the disagreement instead of picking one.
concepts.why: Disagreements between tools, or between widgets in one dashboard, usually reveal a definition or instrumentation gap.

concepts.name: Cost-ordered treatment ladder
concepts.description: Order each reason's treatments from free and low-friction (skip, pause, frequency, education) to swap to paid discount.
concepts.why: Most reasons are not price objections, so discount-first flows spend margin on saves a free option would catch.

concepts.name: Reason-to-treatment mapping
concepts.description: Map each cancel-reason pattern to what it usually means and which treatment should lead.
concepts.why: Makes the recommended flow consistent across clients and explains each choice.

concepts.name: Save-mechanism split
concepts.description: Split saves into offer-claimed and abandonment.
concepts.why: Shows whether offers are doing any work or subscribers are just walking away.

concepts.name: Claim-rate diagnosis
concepts.description: Read per-offer claim rates; a very low rate across offers argues for leaning on free soft-saves.
concepts.why: Stops a recommendation from adding more of what is not converting.

concepts.name: Black-box reason bucket
concepts.description: Flag the largest unclassified reason, such as 'Other', and fix classification before building treatments on it.
concepts.why: It distorts every other share and is usually the top fix.

concepts.name: Replace instead of update
concepts.description: Where a connector cannot edit a file's contents, publish a new file and retire the old one.
concepts.why: A new file has a new link, so bookmarks and shared links to the old one stop working.
